The country’s first urban heatwave action plan has been developed for Narayanganj. National guidelines for dealing with heat-related illness and a public awareness campaign called “Beat the Heat” have also been launched. Courtesy: GHHIN The El Niño phenomenon is strengthening across the Pacific, increasing the risk of another season of extreme heat in South Asia. Against this backdrop, India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan have launched a joint initiative to tackle the impacts of extreme heat. Four new country briefs assessing heatwave conditions, preparedness and gaps in the four countries were released today, Thursday, at the Global Heat Forum, which began in Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, says a press release. The briefs were published under the initiative of the South Asia Hub of the Global Heat Health Information Network (GHHIN). The assessments were conducted as part of a review of countries’ preparedness and capacity as health risks from extreme heat continue to rise across South Asia. The initiative, launched in October 2026, aims to strengthen health surveillance, funding, and local preparedness, according to a media release from the Global Heat Forum. National responses were previously fragmented, but the region now shares a unified evidence base, with assessments highlighting critical gaps in translating heat forecasts into on-the-ground protection. South Asia’s 57% Heat Risk Threshold India’s district-level study reveals 57% of its districts, home to nearly three-quarters of the population, face high to very high heat risk. This aligns with the country’s shift from reactive relief to proactive risk reduction, with over 250 city and district heat action plans in place. Heatwaves are now recognized as a notified natural disaster under India’s disaster risk management funding.
